title: Rotate a list
description: Rotate xs to the left by k positions: the first k elements move to the end, so [1, 2, 3, 4] rotated by 1 is [2, 3, 4, 1]. A negative k rotates to the right ([1, 2, 3, 4] with k = -1 gives [4, 1, 2, 3]), and k may be larger than the length of the list (a full turn changes nothing). An empty list stays empty.
notes: Experiment int_division: hidden tests use negative operands; the description states Euclidean-style non-negative remainder in words. The ref.zehn is written with int.div_floor / int.div_trunc / int.rem_euclid so it is valid under int_ops=operators and int_ops=explicit.
